comment.narrative: Although the project developed 25 communication products since the beginning until 31st Dec 2023 they share messages relevant for each Output where indicator for the development of communication products is associated Output 1.1 1.2 and 2.3. Nevertheless for reporting purposes the split has been made aiming to associate the products to the closest matching Output. In total 2 communication products were registered to this outputs indicator in 2023 as the projects established its 2 social media accounts on LinkedIn and Twitter. The LinkedIn gained 400 followers until the end of 2023 and was quickly adopted as the projects main communication tool producing many impression and often reach to over 2000 accounts in organic way. Many people comment and engage with the projects LinkedIn posts. Twitter on the other hand experienced lower popularity in terms of adoption and engagement. The platforms character limit for posts also prevented the team to share meaningful messages and therefore the accounts future existence is currently in question.

comment.narrative: The main project activities under this output fall under the Aviation Cybersecurity domain and Accident and Incident Investigation where the project identified a great need for regional support and establishing the regional panels. This need has been for the first time expressed by the states during the 1st Project Management Board Meeting PMBM held in the Maldives on 2nd June 2022. Subsequently the project identified the possible way forward and between 2728 June 2022 an Aviation Cybersecurity Workshop was held in Singapore. Unfortunately the project was unable to replicate this achievement in 2023 due to the poor availability of internal EASA experts in the field of cybersecurity who delivered previous Workshops in this domain. To make things worse it has been recommended by EASA not to contract external experts in this field due to the complicated nature of this domain and wait for the availability from the internal resources that have unique knowledge to the topics requested by the South Asian member states.The project management team carefully assessed the situation and for 2024 decided to focus its resources on another domain under this Output Accident and Incident Investigation AII. This topic has been heavily requested by the member states and unlike the Cybersecurity domain it is much more suitable to contract external experts in this domain. Therefore the project manager launched request for services in December 2023 to the external providers of EASA to secure AII expert for the Q1 and Q2 of 2024 to deliver the requested support and to achieve the target of this output.In conclusion there were no activities organised in 2023 contributing towards the target of this indicator. The progress under this outputs indicator remains 25 activities organized as of the 31st Dec 2023.

comment.narrative: The project is conducting feedback surveys with the participants whenever it is necessary possible and appropriate and the surveys are conducted for the meetings with the training and capacity building nature where the participants are expected to benefit from them. Whereas is undoubtedly not up to the project management team to decide which activities are subject to feedback collection and evaluation there are certain activities for which the feedback collection was excluded under this Outputs indicator. Namely this was not necessary and appropriate for the bilateral meetings Gala dinner and Project Management Board Meeting mainly due to the nature of these activities which were of a political networking or coordination nature. Excluded from this indicator are also activities where the EU companies attended them. The feedback from these events is due to the prevention of data duplication instead reported in Output 2.1 as it was prioritised. These activities are those from the series of Coordinated actions of stakeholders with Airbus and Airbus Helicopters EASA SAFE 360 and EUAsia Symposium on UASUAM. The feedback collection for the activity with the title COSCAPSEA EU EASA Mandatory and Voluntary Safety Reporting Systems Workshop was not conducted as this activity was primarily organized by COSCAPSEA where EUSA APP II Project was in the role of support. Therefore it was inappropriate to conduct a feedback survey for such an activity especially considering that it was held online. Additionally it has to be noted that the activities in the SMS domain consisted of many different highly specialized workshops during the experts visits to the beneficiary countries but the feedback was collected from their overall visits output. For instance during the experts visit to India in August 2022 the SMS OJT Preparation Workshop SMS Workshop for Regulators and Industry SMS OJT and SMSSSP Fundamentals Train the Trainer Workshop were all held with the same participants in the span of one week. However the feedback was collected and reported only under the SMSSSP Fundamentals Train the Trainer Workshop as this was the main activity of the visit with all of the participants from the other sessions present in one room. A similar logic has been repeated for the SMS and SSP activities held in Sri Lanka Maldives Pakistan and Bangladesh. SSP Assessment Bhutan was however standalone online activity where the project was unable to collect the feedback results due to the communication difficulty with the beneficiary.The final average feedback collected from the activities in this output came out with 100 satisfaction from the participants where all of them concluded they have benefited from the activities for their daytoday jobrelated tasks. It has to be noted that the participation in the feedback surveys was in all of these cases generous and no results were reported where the survey participation would drop below 25. In fact there was not a single case where the participation would be below 25. The feedback score of 99.19 is well above the targeted 90 target threshold.

title.narrative: Number of EU companies that participated in an event organised/supported

description.narrative: Number of EU companies that participated in an event organised/supported

comment.narrative: Since its commencement till the 31st Dec 2023 the project involved a total of 37 companies from the EU in its activities with the aim to promote EU technologies and best practices and to provide the opportunity to EUbased companies and organizations to showcase and demonstrate their products and services in South Asia. The companies are all from the civil aviation sectors with proficiency in the domains where they were involved. 24 of them have been involved in 2023 alone. The details of the involved companies can be found in the progress report due to the limited space.As described the same issue as for the indicator measuring participation of nonEU companies in the activities organised in relation to the disaggregation applies also for this indicator. The reporting of this Output in OPSYS includes two disaggregation categories. To disaggregate the number of EU companies that participated in an event organised by type of the event by sector of participants in an event and by their gender. Whereas it is straightforward to report the types of event in which the EU companies participated it is unclear what should be reported in the sector of participants in an event. The understanding of the project management team for this scenario would be to gather and analyse attendance sheets of all events where EU companies participated and report a specific sum of numbers of people from each sector for these events. This is however not possible in the current version of OPSYS. The system does not allow to add higher total number in the disaggregation part than the current value of the output. These are two different variables that are mixed in OPSYS. The current value measures the total number of EU companies that participated in the events the projects current value would be 37. However the total number of participants that attended the projects activities where the EU companies participated is far higher than 37 and it cannot be reported due to an error. For this reason it is not possible to report any correct value in the OPSYS disaggregation fields. The reporting follows the method suggested by the contracting authority to overcome this in the 2nd progress report. An estimated ratio was calculated and reported to the OPSYS considering the value of 37 being total instead of 414. The values in this report are reported in as they are more accurate. With this in mind the disaggregation for the activities where EU companies were represented as reported and converted from the percentages in the disaggregation above.

To start the projects ATMANS initiative the experts held bilateral meetings with the individual states to align the expectations and prioritize the area of focus for the upcoming workshops. title.narrative: Number of nonEU companies that participated in the events organised/supported

description.narrative: Number of nonEU companies that participated in the events organised/supportedThis indicator records participation of nonEU companies in an event.

comment.narrative: In total 63 different bodies from the civil aviation industry in South Asia have been reached through the projects activities. The table with the in the 2nd progress report offers the overview of the attending companies organised by country. The predominant part of the list is taken by air operators additionally the project reached also airports air navigation services providers training and maintenance centres as well as accreditation bodies and business and industry development service bodies. All of these companies are in the fields of the projects interest and objectives such as AIR OPS FCL SMS Environment matters Aerodromes and Air Traffic Management.As described in the chapter 5.2.1.5 the same issue as for the indicator measuring participation of EU companies in the activities organised in relation to the disaggregation applies also for this indicator. The reporting of this Output in OPSYS includes three disaggregation categories. To disaggregate the number of nonEU companies that participated in an event organised by type of the event by sector of participants in an event and by their gender. Whereas it is straightforward to report the types of event in which the nonEU companies participated it is unclear what should be reported in the sector of participants in an event and their gender. The understanding of the project management team for this scenario would be to gather and analyse attendance sheets of all events where nonEU companies participated and report a specific sum of numbers of people from each sector for these events as well as their gender. This is however not possible in the current version of OPSYS. The system does not allow to add higher total number in the disaggregation part than the current value of the output. These are two different variables that are mixed in OPSYS. The current value measures the total number of nonEU companies that participated in the events the projects current value would be 63.
